ENVIRONMENT: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: ENVIRONMENT, edition not printed (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/6/Davco%20Ultraflex%20Data%20Sheet.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide ENVIRONMENT where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (edition not printed).
1.2 Product description. Refer to manufacturer. This is not stated in the data sheet reviewed (edition not printed).
1.3 Intended uses. Refer to manufacturer. This is not stated in the data sheet reviewed (edition not printed).

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. ENVIRONMENT
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (edition not printed) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS ISO 13007: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where:  > FEATURES & BENEFITS (p.1);  > General (p.3).
    - SCAQMD method 304-91: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where:  > FEATURES & BENEFITS (p.1).
    - AS3958.1: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where:  > DIRECTIONS FOR USE (p.2).
    - ISO 9001:2008: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where:  > General (p.3).
    - ISO 9001: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where:  > General (p.3).

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 Substrate preparation. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (edition not printed) states no substrate preparation requirements.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (edition not printed) and the requirements below.
4.2 . Premium grade wall and floor cement-based tile adhesive

    Available in a 20kg bag WHERE TO USE Surfaces Most common substrates; cement renders, blockwork and rendered brickwork, plasterboard, fibre cement sheet, compatible waterproofing membranes, timber floors (with fibre cement sheet tile underlay installed), under tile heating, new concrete (cured for 7 days) and new screed (cured for 24 hours). Tiles Ideal for porcelain, ceramic, mosaic, terracotta, slate, quarry, granite and marble. Not suitable for translucent tiles and moisture sensitive stone such as green marble. Areas Suitable for interior and exterior applications. Commercial and domestic walls and floors including living areas, dining areas, walkways, office space, external verandahs and decks.     MIX PREPARATION Mix Process
    1. Measure the right amount of clean, potable water into a clean bucket. 1. Slowly add the powder into the water while mixing with a mixing paddle attached to a drill. Do not mix by hand. 2. Continue to mix for several minutes until a creamy consistency is achieved, free of lumps of powder. 3. Allow mixture to stand for 5 minutes, remix then use the adhesive.
4.5 .
    - 1. Deposit a quantity of adhesive onto the prepared substrate.
    - Do not apply more adhesive than can be tiled within the open time of the product, usually from a single tile up to around 1m² at a time.
    - 2. Hold the notched trowel at an angle of 60º or greater to the substrate.
    - 3. Spread the adhesive over the area where tile is to be applied, forming straight rows of adhesive “beads”.
    - 4. Where “back buttering” is required, use the straight side of the trowel to apply a thin covering of adhesive to the back of the tile.
    - 5. Position the tile on the beaded adhesive and press firmly.
    - 6. Move the tile forward and then back at 90º across the direction of the beads to ensure all beads are flattened leaving no voids under the tile. Occasionally lift a tile after placing it to check that the beads are fully compressed and that sufficient coverage has been achieved (90-100%). Replace the tile.
    - 7. After laying a section at a time, remove any excess adhesive from the surface of the tiles and within the grout joint while the adhesive is still wet.
4.6 .

5.1 Hold point. Before each application, confirm the site conditions with the manufacturer. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions to be verified. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (edition not printed) lists no application condition limits.
5.3 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - • | Test product in an inconspicuous area first
5.4 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.
